xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3294: bug(infra): work-agent-stop-hook has no concurrency guard — dashboard crash-loop fanned out 35 concurrent haiku LLM calls and froze the machine

plan.title: work-agent-stop-hook: single-flight lock, LLM TTL, and machine-wide rate limit
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: A dashboard crash-loop fired the Stop hook chain every ~20s for ~25 min; work-agent-stop-hook has no concurrency cap, no TTL on its `claude -p` completion-check call, and no machine-wide rate limit, so 35 concurrent haiku processes and 70 hook shells accumulated and froze an 8-core/8GB Mac (load 91.81).
narratives.Proposal: Add three portable (macOS+Linux, mkdir-lock, no flock/GNU-timeout dependency) guard primitives to sync-sources/hooks/pan-hook-lib.sh — a per-agent single-flight lock, a pan_run_with_timeout watchdog, and a machine-wide sliding-window token bucket — and wire them into sync-sources/hooks/work-agent-stop-hook: whole-body single-flight per agent, 60s default TTL on the LLM child (env OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT), and a 6-per-minute default machine-wide cap on hook LLM spawns (env OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_RATE_LIMIT). Timeout and rate-limit drops log and exit 0 WITHOUT emitting a resolution so storms cannot ratchet agents to 'stuck'. Full design with verified line references and before/after snippets: .pan/drafts/PAN-3294.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes to other hook scripts (verified audit: work-agent-stop-hook:369 is the only hook LLM spawn today)
- No PAN-2500 memory-governor / server-side integration — guards are pure hook-side bash
- No fix for the dashboard EADDRINUSE crash-loop trigger (separate issue)
- No behavior change for genuine non-timeout claude failures (rc!=0 still falls back to UNCLEAR)
- No migration of existing flock uses (resolution cache, pending-events buffer)
- No config.yaml plumbing for the new knobs (env-only)

autoDecisions.summary: Single-flight lock guards the whole hook body per agent, acquired right after the COMPLETED_FILE early-exit, not just the LLM call.
autoDecisions.rationale: The incident accumulated 70 hook shells beyond the 35 LLM calls; every phase does curl/tmux work, and the issue asks for exit-0-on-live-holder semantics.

autoDecisions.summary: mkdir-based lock directories with pid files instead of flock for all new locking.
autoDecisions.rationale: flock(1) is absent on stock macOS and the incident machine was a Mac; mkdir is atomic on POSIX and works identically on both platforms.

autoDecisions.summary: Timeout default 60s (OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT), rate limit default 6 LLM calls/min machine-wide (OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_RATE_LIMIT), env-only config.
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue sketch suggests ~60s and 'max K per minute'; env-with-hardcoded-default matches the existing OVERDECK_HOOK_TIMEOUT / OVERDECK_COMPLETION_CHECK_MODEL pattern.

autoDecisions.summary: Timeout and rate-limit paths emit NO resolution (exit 0 silently) instead of UNCLEAR.
autoDecisions.rationale: Two consecutive UNCLEAR verdicts escalate to 'stuck'; a storm would mass-flip healthy agents to stuck, creating a second incident. Genuine claude failures keep existing UNCLEAR behavior.

autoDecisions.summary: Guard primitives live in pan-hook-lib.sh; wiring only in work-agent-stop-hook.
autoDecisions.rationale: The requested audit found exactly one LLM-spawning hook; shared-lib placement gives future LLM-calling hooks the same guards without speculative wiring.

autoDecisions.summary: Token bucket fails closed (skips the LLM call) when its lock cannot be acquired.
autoDecisions.rationale: Under contention the machine is by definition busy; spawning fewer LLM processes is the safe direction for a storm breaker.

items.title: Add pan_acquire_singleflight_lock / pan_release_singleflight_lock to pan-hook-lib.sh

expected_outputs: lock-primitive test cases in pan-hook-lib-guards.test.ts pass

narrative.Action: Implement the mkdir-based single-flight lock exactly as specified in PRD WI-1 (.pan/drafts/PAN-3294.md): atomic mkdir of a lock directory, pid file with $$, live-holder check via kill -0, one-shot stale reclaim on dead/unreadable holder, and a release helper. Create tests/scripts/pan-hook-lib-guards.test.ts running the real lib via bash -c, following the mock/temp-dir style of tests/scripts/work-agent-stop-hook.test.ts.

items.title: Given no lock dir, pan_acquire_singleflight_lock creates it, writes the caller PID to <dir>/pid, and returns 0
Given a lock dir whose pid file names a live process, a second acquire returns 1 and preserves the holder's pid file
Given a lock dir whose pid file names a dead PID (or is missing), acquire removes the stale dir, re-creates it, and returns 0
pan_release_singleflight_lock removes the lock directory and returns 0 even when the dir is already gone
Add portable pan_run_with_timeout to pan-hook-lib.sh

expected_outputs: timeout-primitive test cases pass with each test's real wait under 2.5s

narrative.Action: Implement pan_run_with_timeout <secs> <cmd...> per PRD WI-2 / design decision 3: prefer `timeout -k 5`, then `gtimeout -k 5`, else a pure-bash background+watchdog fallback; pass stdin/stdout through (callers use RESULT=$(echo x | pan_run_with_timeout N claude ...)); normalize expiry to rc 124. Subprocess tests use a 1s TTL — vitest fake timers cannot reach a child bash process, so keep real waits ≤2.5s per the hazard H1 note in continue.json.

items.title: A command finishing under the limit returns its own exit code and produces its full stdout through command substitution
pan_run_with_timeout 1 sleep 3 returns 124 within 2.5s of wall clock and leaves no surviving child process
Piped stdin reaches the wrapped command (echo hi | pan_run_with_timeout 5 cat emits hi)
With timeout and gtimeout absent from PATH, the pure-bash fallback still returns 124 on expiry and kills the child
Add machine-wide pan_llm_rate_check token bucket to pan-hook-lib.sh

narrative.Action: Implement pan_llm_rate_check per PRD WI-3 / design decision 5: bucket file ${OVERDECK_HOME:-$HOME/.overdeck}/hook-llm-calls.log with one epoch-seconds line per allowed spawn; under a sibling mkdir lock (hook-llm-calls.lock.d, 10x0.1s bounded acquisition) prune lines older than 60s, return 1 at/over ${OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_RATE_LIMIT:-6}, else append now and return 0; return 1 (fail closed) when the bucket lock cannot be acquired. Tests point OVERDECK_HOME at a temp dir.

items.title: First call with an empty bucket returns 0 and appends exactly one epoch-seconds line to hook-llm-calls.log
Given the bucket pre-filled with limit fresh timestamps, the next call returns 1 and appends nothing
Timestamps older than 60s are pruned from the bucket file and a call after pruning returns 0
With the bucket lock dir held by a live PID, the call returns 1 without modifying the bucket file (fails closed)
Wire the per-agent single-flight guard into work-agent-stop-hook

expected_outputs: concurrency test proves exactly one mock claude spawn for two concurrent invocations

narrative.Action: Insert the PRD WI-4 snippet immediately after the COMPLETED_FILE check (work-agent-stop-hook:47): acquire $AGENT_STATE_DIR/stop-hook.lock.d via pan_acquire_singleflight_lock, exit 0 with a hooks.log skip line when a live holder exists, and trap-release on EXIT. Tests MUST copy the REAL sync-sources/hooks/pan-hook-lib.sh into the temp harness (the existing stub lib would bypass the guard — hazard H6).

items.title: Given two concurrent invocations for one agent with a ~1s mock claude, exactly one claude invocation is logged and both hook processes exit 0
The skipped invocation logs a 'skipped — another instance holds' line to hooks.log and makes no curl or tmux calls after the lock check
Given a leftover lock dir whose pid file names a dead PID, the next invocation reclaims it and spawns the LLM check (mock claude log gains a line)
A normal completed run exits with the lock directory removed (trap released it)
Wrap the claude call with TTL and machine-wide rate check in work-agent-stop-hook

expected_outputs: timeout and rate-limit tests pass with zero resolution events in the mock heartbeat log

narrative.Action: Apply the PRD WI-5 before/after replacement at work-agent-stop-hook:368-375: pan_llm_rate_check gate (log 'rate-limited' and exit 0 on refusal), then RESULT=$(echo "$ANALYSIS_PROMPT" | pan_run_with_timeout "${OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT:-60}" claude -p --model "$COMPLETION_MODEL" 2>>"$CLAUDE_STDERR"); rc 124/137/143 logs 'timed out' and exits 0 with no resolution emitted. Keep the existing non-timeout rc!=0 -> UNCLEAR fallback byte-for-byte. Tests use OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT=1 with a 3s-sleeping mock claude and a pre-filled bucket.

items.title: With OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT=1 and a mock claude sleeping 3s, the hook exits 0 in under 2.5s, emits zero heartbeat resolution events, and logs 'timed out' to hooks.log
With the token bucket pre-filled to the limit, the hook exits 0 without invoking mock claude and logs 'rate-limited' to hooks.log
Under the limit with a fast mock claude answering FORGOT_COMPLETION, the hook still emits resolution done and the bucket file gains one line
A non-timeout claude failure (rc=1) still falls back to the UNCLEAR verdict path exactly as before
Document the hook LLM guardrails in docs/HOOKS.md

expected_outputs: grep count is at least 2 (both env vars documented)

narrative.Action: Add a '## Hook LLM Guardrails (PAN-3294)' section to docs/HOOKS.md after '## Hook Scripts Inventory' per PRD WI-6: the three guards, env vars OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT (default 60) and OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_RATE_LIMIT (default 6/min), the no-resolution-on-timeout/drop rule and its unclear->stuck rationale, on-disk paths (<agent dir>/stop-hook.lock.d, ~/.overdeck/hook-llm-calls.log), and the incident reference. Update the work-agent-stop-hook row in the inventory table to mention the guards.

items.title: docs/HOOKS.md contains a Hook LLM Guardrails section naming OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_TIMEOUT with default 60 and OVERDECK_HOOK_LLM_RATE_LIMIT with default 6 per minute
The section contains the no-resolution-on-timeout/drop rule and shows both on-disk paths (stop-hook.lock.d and hook-llm-calls.log)
The Hook Scripts Inventory row for work-agent-stop-hook shows the single-flight, TTL, and rate-limit guards
